risks: §9.7 cites many existing constructs that cannot be verified from the prompt alone (§9.5 moot reason codes `no_longer_relevant`, `invalidated_by_universe_change`, `user_declared_moot`; §7.4.1 routine occurrence controls; §17.0 decision payload; §17.3 correction links; `elapsed_time`/`log_review_due` paths; Setting vs Preference distinction). Any of these being absent or named differently would leave dangling references.

The proposal maps the question's 'cancel permanently' option onto the existing terminal `moot` status and explicitly forbids a `cancelled` status, while the replaced DESIGN.md paragraph previously spoke of 'cancelled (which is terminal)'. If the Task model actually has a distinct cancelled status, this introduces a contradiction rather than a clarification.

Promotion to active requires citing an enabled, user-accepted pairwise Preference. If ordinary Task admission does not require a Preference at creation, promoted Tasks are held to a stricter bar than newly created active Tasks, which is an asymmetry the text does not acknowledge.

The §9.7 text is very dense (idempotency keys, sync coalescing, Compartment/Replica caveats, multi-clause `next_review_at` recomputation rule). It is hard to audit and some sentences are difficult to parse, raising the chance of later misreading or conflicting interpretation.

Several implementation-flavoured details (exact idempotency key tuples, 2592000-second default, per-episode coalescing) are specified in a design document; they are consistent with the §9.6/UBU-D0307 pattern but lock in choices that may better belong to a later implementation decision.
scores.rationale: The patch applies cleanly, touches only the three allowlisted files, and sets `Status: Solved` with `Resolved by: UBU-D0308` while preserving all other question metadata. It answers all five subquestions directly: (1) a single `deferred_intent` record with episode id, entry time, optional reason, optional tagged defer-until boundary, interval, last/next review, and an explicit user deferral action; (2) full exclusion before kernel dispatch including gap-fill and transitive dependents, i.e. the 'invisible' option, with no TaskSpec change; (3) new `task_deferred_intent_entered/updated/exited` events plus `decision_recorded` with `decision_kind: deferred_intent_review`; (4) a 30-day default surfaced on Log review or startup, postponed by defer_until, pulled earlier by material linked-Objective changes, with manual review always available; (5) promote, keep deferred, dismiss via `moot`, or Objective review. It follows the structure of the adjacent §9.6/UBU-D0307 waiting lifecycle, appends a single new decision in sequence, allocates no new questions, and updates the §17.8 Log-review bullet coherently. The current direction (Preference requirement enforced at review rather than creation) is honoured. Deductions are for unverifiable cross-references, the `cancelled`-to-`moot` reinterpretation, the promotion-stricter-than-creation asymmetry, and the density of the new section, which hurts auditability.
